target.title: refactor(memory): move QMD coordination to SQLite
target.body:
Related: #66339

## What Problem This Solves

QMD runtime writes were still coordinated with lock sidecar files. Gateway and CLI processes can update and embed the same QMD index, so stale sidecars, process pauses, and split cleanup ownership could either block healthy work or allow SQLite writer contention. The sidecars also violated the database-first storage contract for OpenClaw-owned runtime state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves QMD coordination to host-owned SQLite leases: the shared state database serializes global embedding capacity, while each agent database serializes writes to that agent's QMD index. Leases use bounded asynchronous admission, expiry/heartbeat renewal, exact-owner checkpoints, WAL-compatible reads, and fail-closed cancellation. Runtime no longer reads or writes QMD lock files.

Doctor removes only the two exact retired sidecar shapes when they are unchanged, stale regular files. Snapshot and backup paths remove transient lease rows without mutating source databases. The upgrade boundary is a clean restart of all processes sharing the state directory; there is no dual-lock or runtime fallback path.

QMD's YAML configuration, index database, and model cache remain QMD-owned artifacts. Upstream QMD source was inspected at `tobi/qmd@e428df76bc0274d9e93eb7ca3e95673315c42e90` to confirm that OpenClaw must serialize the external update/embed writers at the host boundary.

## User Impact

Operators get cross-process QMD write coordination through the canonical SQLite stores, with no OpenClaw-owned lock sidecars. Lease rows are transient and excluded from backups and snapshots. After upgrading, all processes sharing one state directory must be restarted before QMD work resumes.

## Evidence

- Current-base focused proof: 374 Memory Core QMD/session-artifact tests passed; 147 lease/agent-database/snapshot/backup tests passed with 2 skipped.
- Final overlap proof: 19 lease/runtime-binding tests passed after combining the latest trusted-plugin ingress-drain and lease surfaces.
- Exact-head CI [29555891078](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29555891078): all 71 jobs passed at `1e5d8a7a5f3e506c2d0d694c9ea44557955d37c6`.
- Testbox changed gate [29553368420](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29553368420): generators, SDK budgets, plugin boundaries, all core/extension/test-root typechecks, and core/extension lint passed. The run stopped only on the then-current `main` duplicate release-checklist declaration, fixed by `225638788572`; targeted script lint passes on the rebased head.
- Fresh `autoreview` clean on the exact CI head after the final rebase.
- `git diff --check`, Kysely/database-first guards, SDK budgets, and generated SQLite/Plugin SDK baselines clean.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the lease, migration, doctor, snapshot, and backup paths changed here.

target.title: fix(gateway): multi-account channel stops no longer fan out unbounded
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping or reloading a channel with many configured accounts could launch every provider teardown hook at once. A six-account reproduction reached six concurrent stop hooks, and a slow hook could run before later account runtimes had even received their abort signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whole-channel stops now abort every selected account first, then run provider stop hooks and the existing graceful task wait with the same four-account concurrency bound already used for account startup. Grace deadlines start at abort time so queued accounts keep the same five-second stop window, and queued teardown work is fenced from any newer replacement runtime. Single-account behavior, timeout state, and public configuration are unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdowns and channel reloads avoid unbounded account teardown bursts while still cancelling all affected runtimes immediately. Large multi-account channel configurations no longer multiply provider cleanup concurrency.

## Evidence

- Regression RED on the previous implementation: the six-account test reported `expected 4, received 6`; stop hooks observed abort counts `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]` instead of all six accounts already being aborted.
- Immediate abort ordering: the green regression requires all six aborts to be visible before the first stop hook and requires every hook to observe an abort count of six.
- Bounded teardown: the green regression requires a first wave of four active stop hooks, a second wave of two, and a maximum concurrency of four.
- Shared deadline: a six-account stalled-task regression requires the whole stop to finish at the first five-second grace deadline rather than adding another deadline for queued accounts.
- Replacement fencing: a queued-teardown regression starts a replacement for account five and verifies that stale teardown neither calls its stop hook nor marks the replacement runtime stopped.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` — 51 tests passed on `4c3d851746027a293236e58cbe0080a2a5d73258`. Gateway benchmark before: Vitest 132.05s / wrapper wall 147.19s (48 tests, cold transform). Final: Vitest 31.66s; wrapper wall 381.08s included 5m31s queued behind another worktree's shared heavy-check lock, so the timing delta is not presented as a performance claim.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/gateway/server-channels.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts`

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): stop oversized streaming TTS audio
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ElevenLabs streaming TTS could continue delivering provider audio beyond the 16 MiB audio limit already enforced by the buffered TTS path. An oversized or unbounded response could therefore keep consuming playback and network resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ElevenLabs stream owner now applies a non-buffering cumulative byte guard using the existing `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` policy. It forwards at most the allowed bytes, reports a stable overflow error, and cancels the upstream response without adding configuration or changing the public API.

## User Impact

Normal ElevenLabs streaming TTS completes with the same bytes and completion semantics. Oversized streams stop at 16 MiB instead of continuing without a bound.

## Evidence

### Recorded RED → GREEN boundary proof

Before the production fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/tts.test.ts` produced the expected RED:

```text
FAIL  extensions/elevenlabs/tts.test.ts > cancels streamed audio before delivering bytes beyond the audio limit
AssertionError: promise resolved "{ value: Uint8Array[ 1 ], done: false }" instead of rejecting
Tests  1 failed | 12 passed
```

This demonstrates the previous stream handed the `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES + 1` byte to the consumer.

On the final reviewed diff:

- Focused regression: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-elevenlabs-review-fix ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-media.config.ts extensions/elevenlabs/tts.test.ts` — 1 file and 13 tests passed.
- Plugin lane: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-elevenlabs-extension-review-fix ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-media.config.ts extensions/elevenlabs` — 5 files and 34 tests passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/elevenlabs/tts.ts extensions/elevenlabs/tts.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/elevenlabs/tts.ts extensions/elevenlabs/tts.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

### Mapping to the requested proof

- **Normal completion:** the streaming endpoint test consumes the returned stream, observes bytes `[1, 2, 3]`, then observes `{ done: true }`.
- **Controlled overflow and cleanup:** the overflow test consumes exactly `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES`, verifies the next read rejects with `ElevenLabs API error: audio response exceeds 16777216 bytes`, and verifies the upstream stream's `cancel` callback runs once.
- **Actual OpenClaw consumer / live ElevenLabs setup:** not run. These tests use a real Web `ReadableStream` through the canonical `elevenLabsTTSStream` owner, but replace network fetch with a test response. This PR does not claim live provider or end-to-end consumer proof.

target.title: fix(reef): repeated relay reconnects no longer leave stale sockets active
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated Reef relay reconnects could retain abort listeners from earlier WebSocket generations. Local frame-processing failures could also leave an abandoned socket connected after its replacement started, causing listener warnings over time and stale socket activity during channel shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Reef inbox WebSocket generation now owns a named abort listener that is removed on its first terminal transition. Generations that fail locally are closed before replacement, while the existing reconnect, backoff, and remote-close behavior remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running Reef channels can reconnect repeatedly without accumulating shutdown listeners or retaining failed sockets. Channel abort now closes only the active WebSocket generation.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new two-generation regression observed two abort listeners after the first generation settled; the expected bound is one active listener.
- The final controlled regression verifies that malformed input closes the failed generation, the replacement is the only generation subscribed to channel abort, and abort does not close the failed generation again.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts --run` — 14 tests passed.
- `node scripts/test-extension.mjs reef` — completed the Reef extension plan covering 23 test files.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/reef/src/transport.ts extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts` — passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/reef/src/transport.ts extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts` — passed.

### Proof boundary and remaining action

No run against a real Reef relay was performed. The evidence above uses the production reconnect loop with controlled WebSocket generations and does not claim to prove real-relay close-event ordering. Clearing the current `needs proof` rating requires a redacted real-relay run demonstrating repeated reconnect generations, one active abort listener, and closure of a locally failed socket.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

target.title: fix(cli): oversized secrets plans consume unbounded memory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw secrets apply --from <path>` could make the CLI fully allocate and parse an arbitrarily large plan file before its shape was validated. A 32 MiB valid JSON file reached plan validation instead of being rejected at the file boundary, creating avoidable memory pressure before either dry-run or mutation could begin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The serialized plan boundary now caps files at 16 MiB, verifies the opened target is a regular file, and reads the pinned descriptor through the existing bounded file reader. This also exposes the limit in `--from` help. Plan schema, target validation, provider behavior, and apply semantics are unchanged.

A fresh semantic recall checked 26 open pull requests. The closest changes improve malformed-JSON and missing-file diagnostics in the same reader, but neither bounds successful file reads.

## User Impact

Oversized secrets plans now fail early with a clear byte-limit error instead of being fully loaded and parsed. Normal plans generated by `openclaw secrets configure --plan-out` continue through dry-run and apply unchanged.

## Evidence

Real CLI proof on the fixed commit:

```text
$ openclaw secrets apply --from small-plan.json --dry-run
Secrets apply dry run: no changes.
exit=0

$ openclaw secrets apply --from 32MiB-plan.json --dry-run
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file exceeds 16777216 bytes: ...
exit=1
```

The 32 MiB fixture was valid JSON (whitespace followed by `{}`), and the output did not reach the previous `Invalid secrets plan file` diagnostic. The same real CLI check on the pinned latest-main snapshot still reached `Invalid secrets plan file`, confirming the problem remained upstream before this patch.

Focused validation:

```text
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       16 passed (16)

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --quiet src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts
exit=0
```

The regression drives the real Commander action with a file one byte over the limit and verifies `runSecretsApply` is never called. Gateway startup was not part of the proof because plan loading is completed by the standalone CLI before apply or any Gateway interaction begins.

target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
Related: #103720
Supersedes #104085.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where natural-language assistant responses to heartbeat polls could enter the Dreaming session corpus. The existing sanitizer removed the heartbeat user marker and exact heartbeat acknowledgments, but retained arbitrary assistant text generated during the same heartbeat turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Heartbeat turns now persist the existing internal-system provenance with a heartbeat source-tool marker. Session corpus construction uses that trusted runtime fact to exclude every assistant response in the heartbeat turn until the next user turn.

This does not add a new provenance kind, and user-authored heartbeat-like text cannot suppress an assistant response. Historical transcripts do not contain an authenticated heartbeat marker, so this change intentionally does not guess from text or delete existing corpus lines.

## User Impact

New heartbeat responses no longer add low-value Dreaming memories. Normal user turns, media-only turns, and inter-session turns remain indexable. Existing Dreaming diaries and ingestion checkpoints are untouched.

## Evidence

- Focused regression proof: 140 tests passed across session corpus construction and prepared-reply persistence.
- Covers multiple assistant responses separated by tool activity, user-spoofed heartbeat text, media-only next turns, and inter-session next turns.

target.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents
target.body:
## Summary

- preflight each exact, version-pinned ClawHub package as install or reuse and bind that owner decision into the consented plan
- revalidate plugin owner state immediately before mutation, then use the existing skill and plugin installer surfaces
- persist pending, complete, or failed package provenance so partial installs and independently owned packages remain explainable
- return structured partial results when a package or later agent/config mutation fails after package work has begun
- warn across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI plugin removal when any Claw provenance, including uncertain provenance, references the plugin

## Scope

This is the package-owner slice of the experimental Claw lifecycle. It keeps the grouped RFC contract (`packages[].kind`, `source`, `ref`, and exact `version`) and deliberately does not restore generic artifact selectors or agent skill lists. MCP servers and cron jobs remain blocked for later stack slices.

The dry-run records whether each package is absent or already present at the exact version. Apply requires the matching plan digest and rechecks plugin owner state before invoking the installer, so a package cannot silently change from Claw-installed to independently owned, or the reverse, after consent. Package work runs before agent/config/workspace mutation; any later collision returns a partial result that retains the package evidence.

Package references describe dependency provenance, not exclusive ownership. An exact package reused from the operator is recorded as independently owned. A Claw-started install is recorded before external mutation and transitions from pending to complete or failed. Existing experimental databases receive the new update timestamp through an additive migration. Plugin uninstall remains operator-controlled but warns for complete and uncertain Claw references.

The CLI remains process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` in the base of this stack.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #101973 managed workspace files
- This PR: package owner preflight, installers, provenance, and shared uninstall warnings
- Next: #102296 status and remove

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- focused Oxlint on changed Claw, plugin, and state files
- 47 focused package, provenance, plugin-uninstall, and state-database tests
- 6 Claw lifecycle E2E tests
- `codex-review --mode local` clean after addressing additive migration, error preservation, and uncertain-reference warning findings

target.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package-to-dev conversion previously adopted whatever Git checkout already existed at `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. A checkout could retain a canonical-looking URL while using `skipFetchAll`, a hostile fetch refspec, a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref, executable local Git config, or URL rewriting to influence what the updater built and globally installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remote validation cannot make an adopted checkout safe. Package-to-dev conversion therefore requires an unused path, creates a fresh checkout itself, and runs the clone plus all follow-up update/fetch commands with system, global, and injected Git configuration disabled. Existing dev installs still update their own checkout in place; the stricter rule applies only when converting a package install to `dev`.

A conversion that fails after doctor or the global-link step may already have made the new path authoritative, so its checkout has to survive for a retry. Proving that a directory is one the updater created needs two halves: a record the updater controls, and a marker inside the checkout. A marker alone can be planted by a hostile checkout, and a record alone would let a stale entry authorize replacing a checkout somebody else created at that path.

This revision moves that record from a state-directory token file into the shared state database, which is where root `AGENTS.md` requires OpenClaw-owned runtime and recovery state to live. It also fixes the ordering the token file made visible. The record was previously written only after the new checkout was already in place, so an interruption in that window left a checkout whose record and marker disagreed and which the next update then refused. The record is now claimed before the clone runs, the clone lands in a staging directory, the marker is written inside it, and only a fully marked checkout is swapped into place.

## User Impact

- `openclaw update --channel dev` from a package install requires an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.
- Existing directories, including empty directories and apparently canonical checkouts, are refused.
- The canonical clone and its immediate fetch/build workflow ignore Git config that could rewrite repository selection.
- A conversion interrupted partway can be run again. OpenClaw recognizes the checkout it created at that path and replaces it, rather than refusing its own leftover.
- Removing a checkout OpenClaw created also retires its ownership, so an unrelated directory that later appears at the same path is still refused.
- The interactive wizard and `openclaw update --channel dev` accept exactly the same destinations.
- Existing Git/dev installations are unchanged.

## Regression Coverage

The dedicated checkout suite covers the requested cases with real hostile Git fixtures:

- canonical URL plus `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true` and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a hostile fetch refspec and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref;
- injected/global Git configuration that rewrites the canonical URL;
- existing empty directories;
- clone/update/global-link failures and managed retry replacement.

Interrupted state transitions are covered explicitly:

- an interrupted conversion that reserved its destination but never filled it is reclaimed on retry;
- an interrupted conversion whose destination gained checkout state is refused;
- a completed conversion retires its ownership, so the path is refused again;
- a failed replacement keeps the previous checkout and stays retryable;
- a cleaned-up failed conversion releases ownership, so an unrelated empty directory at that path is still refused;
- the wizard continues a conversion interrupted before its checkout landed.

The command-level suite also verifies refusal occurs before service mutation, follow-up fetches receive the sanitized Git environment, failed initial conversions clean up safely, service-repair-aware failures retain a usable target, and successful conversion retires retry ownership.

## Evidence

Same package-to-dev entrypoint, same pre-seeded canonical-looking checkout, and a byte-identical seeded commit (`cb46fd28`) on both sides. Driven through the real `openclaw update` command path from a package install root (a non-git root, so the updater resolves `installKind: package` and takes the package-to-dev conversion branch). Private paths are replaced with placeholders.

Hostile fixture in both runs: canonical `remote.origin.url`, `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true`, a pre-seeded `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and a `PAYLOAD.txt` the canonical repository does not contain.

```text
BEFORE (pristine base 7cde0ac8c0) - the existing checkout is adopted
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.skipFetchAll
true
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main
cb46fd28114f2f92783c352b390506b416720e7f
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 9999.0.0

Steps:
  OK   clean check (12ms)
  OK   git fetch (15ms)
  FAIL git show-ref main (10ms)
      fatal: 'refs/heads/main' - not a valid ref
  OK   git remote (9ms)
  FAIL upstream check (10ms)
      fatal: no such branch: 'main'
  OK   git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (11ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (20ms)
  OK   preflight checkout (cb46fd28) (12ms)
  OK   preflight deps install (cb46fd28) (402ms)
  FAIL preflight build (cb46fd28) (403ms)
  OK   preflight cleanup (11ms)

Total time: 1.82s
```

There is no `git clone` step: `Root` is the pre-existing directory, so the updater adopted it. `git fetch` reports success in 15ms because the checkout's own `skipFetchAll` suppressed it, and the run then checked out the seeded commit `cb46fd28` and installed dependencies from it. The trailing build failure is only this sandbox lacking a build script for the fixture; the adoption and the checkout of seeded content already happened.

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d, identical inputs) - refused before any mutation
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Error: OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR already exists: <private>/checkout. Package-to-dev conversion
creates a fresh OpenClaw checkout and will not reuse existing directories. Move it or
set OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR to an unused path.
    at reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:249:13)
    at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
  [cause]: Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '<private>/checkout'
      at async reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:243:5)
      at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
      at async runGitUpdate (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:456:7)
      at async updateCommandInternal (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:1211:11)
      at async updateCommand (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:583:10)
    errno: -17, code: 'EEXIST', syscall: 'mkdir', path: '<private>/checkout'

$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR log --oneline -1
cb46fd2 seed hostile checkout
$ ls $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR
PAYLOAD.txt package.json
```

The refusal comes from the reservation `mkdir` inside `createGitCheckout`, before any step runs against the directory, and the pre-existing checkout is left exactly as it was.

Same head, unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, showing the reordered crash-safe conversion:

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d) - fresh path clones for real
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/unused-checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 2026.7.2

Steps:
  OK   git clone (174s)
  OK   clean check (1.2s)
  OK   git fetch (824ms)

  OK   preflight checkout (a06799ab) (940ms)
  FAIL preflight deps install (a06799ab) (36.36s)
  [9 further preflight checkout / deps install pairs elided; each install failed identically]
  OK   preflight cleanup (3.19s)

Total time: 324.47s
```

Observed while that clone was still running: the destination is reserved but still empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded in the shared state database.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent

.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329

$ du -sh <private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout <private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-*

$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
[{"plugin_id":"core:update-cli","namespace":"managed-checkouts","value_json":"{\"token\":\"3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e\",\"dir\":\"<private>/unused-checkout\",\"createdAtMs\":1784258040670}"}]
```


That conversion still ends in `ERROR` because dependency installation cannot run in this sandbox. The failure exercised the recovery path: the updater removed the checkout it had created and retired its ownership record, leaving nothing adopted.

Driven through the same package-to-dev conversion path on this head, with a real clone of the canonical remote, an isolated state directory, and an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. Nothing in `update-cli` is mocked. Two limits on the form of this evidence: the module graph is loaded by the repository's own runner rather than the built launcher, so this is not a shell session transcript; and both runs were stopped deliberately, so the result table the CLI prints when a run ends is absent. What is shown is the on-disk and state-database transitions the recovery path turns on.

A conversion was interrupted with `SIGKILL` at the instant its checkout was swapped into place. Observed while its clone was still running, the destination is reserved but empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded:

```text
.
```

```text
unused-checkout
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1

```

```text
ls: cannot access '<private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt': No such file or directory
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
```

target.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents
target.body:
## Summary

- preflight each exact, version-pinned ClawHub package as install or reuse and bind that owner decision into the consented plan
- revalidate plugin owner state immediately before mutation, then use the existing skill and plugin installer surfaces
- persist pending, complete, or failed package provenance so partial installs and independently owned packages remain explainable
- return structured partial results when a package or later agent/config mutation fails after package work has begun
- warn across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI plugin removal when any Claw provenance, including uncertain provenance, references the plugin

## Scope

This is the package-owner slice of the experimental Claw lifecycle. It keeps the grouped RFC contract (`packages[].kind`, `source`, `ref`, and exact `version`) and deliberately does not restore generic artifact selectors or agent skill lists. MCP servers and cron jobs remain blocked for later stack slices.

The dry-run records whether each package is absent or already present at the exact version. Apply requires the matching plan digest and rechecks plugin owner state before invoking the installer, so a package cannot silently change from Claw-installed to independently owned, or the reverse, after consent. Package work runs before agent/config/workspace mutation; any later collision returns a partial result that retains the package evidence.

Package references describe dependency provenance, not exclusive ownership. An exact package reused from the operator is recorded as independently owned. A Claw-started install is recorded before external mutation and transitions from pending to complete or failed. Existing experimental databases receive the new update timestamp through an additive migration. Plugin uninstall remains operator-controlled but warns for complete and uncertain Claw references.

The CLI remains process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` in the base of this stack.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #101973 managed workspace files
- This PR: package owner preflight, installers, provenance, and shared uninstall warnings
- Next: #102296 status and remove

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- focused Oxlint on changed Claw, plugin, and state files
- 47 focused package, provenance, plugin-uninstall, and state-database tests
- 6 Claw lifecycle E2E tests
- `codex-review --mode local` clean after addressing additive migration, error preservation, and uncertain-reference warning findings

target.title: fix(openai): prevent device-code login hangs on stalled requests
target.body:
Related: #104477

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI device-code login could remain stuck indefinitely when an `auth.openai.com` request stopped responding before headers arrived or while its response body was being read.

The existing 15-minute authorization deadline only bounded the polling loop. A single user-code, poll, or token-exchange request could outlive that deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three device-code operations now use the canonical guarded OAuth HTTP lifecycle with a 30-second per-operation deadline, caller cancellation, HTTPS enforcement, audit context, bounded response reads, and deterministic resource release. Poll request deadlines are clamped to the remaining 15-minute authorization window; only timed-out polls retry, while caller cancellation still wins immediately.

When `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` applies to an OpenAI auth URL, the request selects the same trusted environment-proxy guarded mode used by Google OAuth. `NO_PROXY` matches retain strict guarded fetch. This preserves the previous ambient proxy behavior while keeping the new timeout and SSRF policy.

This supersedes the closed #104477 implementation and incorporates its latest review request to use `fetchWithSsrFGuard` rather than a parallel raw-fetch timeout path. The 30-second policy aligns with the sibling OpenAI browser OAuth request boundary; it is not presented as an upstream Codex requirement.

## User Impact

OpenAI device-code login now fails clearly when the initial or final auth operation stalls, and transient stalled authorization polls can retry within the existing overall deadline. Ctrl-C and other caller cancellation behavior remains unchanged. Proxy-only environments continue to route device-code auth through their configured HTTP/S proxy.

No configuration, public API, endpoint, or happy-path authentication behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Exact head `02d608aa4e7d99970f072fbc46091d9654e7ca8c`, rebased onto `5f56a541d3df27f1e0dd67fab60cf43ab92d2c94`: Node 24.18.0 focused suite `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts` passed 15/15.
- Controlled production-path transport proof used `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` with its default fetch, a local CONNECT proxy, and a locally trusted `auth.openai.com` test certificate. The proxy observed `CONNECT auth.openai.com:443` and `POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode` in both cases.
- Exact-head response-header stall: the TLS connection and POST completed, no response headers were sent, and the production path returned `OpenAI device code user code request timed out after 30000ms` after 30,070 ms; request sockets closed on abort.
- Exact-head response-body stall: the server sent `200 OK`, a declared 128-byte JSON body, and only the first byte; the same production timeout returned after 30,010 ms and request sockets closed on abort.
- Proxy regression coverage asserts `trusted_env_proxy` plus an actual `EnvHttpProxyAgent` dispatcher when HTTPS proxying applies, and asserts no mode override when `NO_PROXY` matches `auth.openai.com`.
- Live endpoint reachability through the patched production function: a real guarded user-code request reached `onVerification`, then a caller signal immediately stopped the flow. Redacted output: `{"verified":true,"cancelledAfterVerification":true}`. No user code, device id, or credentials were emitted.
- Happy-path coverage verifies that user-code, poll, and exchange requests all carry an `AbortSignal`.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head repository CI is authoritative for the broader plugin-SDK/type lanes.
- Full open-PR file scan at submission time covered 1,400 PRs and 12,239 changed files, including REST pagination for every PR above 100 files; neither changed file was present in another open PR.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the exact head found no actionable issue after checking the proxy compatibility repair, SSRF/timeout/body lifecycle, callers, sibling OpenAI OAuth path, tests, and sibling Codex source.
- Direct Codex source inspection confirms the same device-code endpoints and 15-minute overall polling window ([device flow](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs#L62-L108)); its HTTP client exposes a per-request timeout API but does not prescribe 30 seconds ([client API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/http-client/src/default_client.rs#L129-L131)).

target.title: fix(reef): add timeout and bounded JSON reads to relay transport
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Reef relay transport client (`extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`) calls `fetch` with no timeout. A relay that black-holes the TCP/TLS handshake or stalls before returning headers will hang `ReefInboxConnection.drain()` forever, silently killing the reconnect/backoff loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the same pattern as recent merged fixes that bound network operations (e.g., #106035, #105885, #102865). The change wraps relay requests in `fetchWithTimeout` (15 s) using the existing injectable `fetcher`, so tests can stub stalled responses. Bounded JSON response reads already landed on `main` via #106456 (16 MiB success / 64 KiB error caps through `readProviderJsonResponse`); this PR adds only the missing request timeout on top of them.

## User Impact

- Prevents silent channel death when the Reef relay becomes unresponsive.
- No behavior change for healthy relays; a stall surfaces as a `TimeoutError` at the 15 s deadline and triggers the existing reconnect path.

## Evidence

- New test covers a stalled relay timing out after 15 s; existing main-side tests cover the bounded JSON reads.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts --run` — 10/10 tests passed on the exact head.
- Exact-head controlled-relay proof (real loopback HTTP+WS server, no fetch mocks): healthy pull succeeds; a stalled pre-header request aborts at 15080 ms with `TimeoutError`; a 16 MiB+1 JSON body is rejected with `reef.relay: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`; after relay 500s the inbox backoff loop recovers, drains the backlog, connects the live socket, and receives the pushed entry. Full transcript in the comments.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 12:47 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:47 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 17, 2026, 12:44 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:44 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@19b5e564d7e363a6249e1704f3363eff81395305`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 04:44 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@19b5e564d7e363a6249e1704f3363eff81395305`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@3318791c33d39118494c0dd85c6be64b93c52c60`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`
- focused gateway session/startup and subagent tests selected by changed-file CI
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/agents/command/model-selection.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`

## Evidence Source Map

- Current patch-head CI: [patch workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29555662547)
  - Checkout target: `3318791c33d39118494c0dd85c6be64b93c52c60`
  - Base: `19b5e564d7e363a6249e1704f3363eff81395305`

  - All contribution-owned format, lint, type, agent-command, subagent, reply-model-selection, and gateway lanes passed.
  - The sole root failure was Control UI i18n catalog baseline drift outside this PR's changed files; the current base/patch pair above provides the final attribution check.
- Initial exact-head run: [initial evidence workflow](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29553799447) (failed)
  - Found and fixed two contribution-owned issues: one `oxfmt` difference and one complete-module test mock missing the new helper export.
- Draft-state upstream PR CI: [PR workflow run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29554005118)
  - Conclusion: skipped as expected while the PR is Draft; a full PR run will replace this entry before review is requested.

## Sanitized Logs

```text
Merged config: listed agent without thinkingDefault -> global value
Explicit override: listed agent thinkingDefault=off -> off
Precedence guard: listed agent without override + per-model thinking + global default -> per-model value
git diff --check -> passed
```

No credentials, hostnames, internal paths, account identifiers, or private
runtime data are included.

## Media Evidence

This is a non-visual configuration-resolution change. The linked Actions run
provides the complete reproducible source-level flow and exact-head result;
there is no UI state or dynamic interaction for a screenshot or recording to
clarify.

## Risk

- Compatibility: callers that intentionally inspect merged config now observe
  the documented global fallback.
- Precedence: mitigated by keeping explicit agent provenance in a dedicated
  helper and by regression coverage for per-model-over-global behavior.
- Performance: one normalized agent-entry lookup replaces an equivalent config
  lookup at the affected callers; no new I/O or runtime catalog loading.
- Security/privacy: no authorization, secret, persistence, or transport changes.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No schema migration, persisted-data rewrite, config migration,
or irreversible operation is introduced.

## Documentation Updated

No documentation change is required. `docs/tools/thinking.md` and the config

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` retain a five-second launcher deadline;
- Linux `xdg-open` runs detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`, while the gateway observes only the first five seconds for immediate launcher failures;
- a long-lived Linux foreground handler is treated as launched and is never killed.

The configuration-specific lifecycle is isolated in `config-open.ts`; the shared `open-path.ts` contract used by session workspace reveal remains unchanged.

## User Impact

The `config.openFile` RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures retain the existing actionable response. macOS and Windows launcher waits remain bounded.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `55f04309cea509a0cae81fe1cdbc88f53ff53643` on current `origin/main` `96815a437b33872ee55c70c4fb10eb7e5c942506`.
- Node 24.18.0 focused suite: `src/gateway/server-methods/config-open.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`, 36/36 tests passed.
- Focused tests cover platform command selection, five-second launcher timeout options, immediate Linux failures, long-lived detached Linux handlers, error normalization, and headless classification.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed on all four changed files.
- Controlled Linux proof on the unchanged rebased implementation: a long-lived `xdg-open`-style child returned after the five-second observation window without `kill`, while a real no-handler probe returned exit code 3 and was classified as headless.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the final lifecycle found no actionable runtime bug; Execa 9.6.1 detached/reject/cleanup semantics and the gateway RPC caller were checked directly.

Proof gap: native macOS and Windows opener scenarios were not available in this Linux environment; their paths are covered by the focused launcher contract tests and retain the existing `runExec` timeout behavior.

AI-assisted: yes. No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.

target.title: fix(xai): bound stalled generated video download body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where xAI generated-video downloads had no download-owned chunk-idle timeout on the success body reader. A mid-body stall only surfaced as a generic guarded-fetch `request timed out` (or waited the full request budget) instead of a clear download idle failure. Google's sibling path already passes `chunkTimeoutMs` / `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadXaiVideo`, pass `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, matching `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts` (`downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri`).

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever on this path; the idle bound is the missing download-owned stall signal. Shared fetch/assert helpers are unchanged.

Non-overlapping: #108982 is a multi-provider video download batch and does not include xAI. #108796 is TTS WebSocket handshake tests only.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadXaiVideo` / `extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts`.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI generated-video downloads fail with `xAI generated video download stalled after <timeout>ms` instead of only a generic request timeout. Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3be32a49ac55d3adef9f757f30b0e00086cd0c72`
`oxfmt --check extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ rejects a stalled body with the download-owned idle timeout 3460ms
 ✓ rejects a continuously dripping CDN body within the guarded request deadline 354ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 417ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Loopback proof

- **Stalled body**: mock fetch, real `readResponseWithLimit` with `chunkTimeoutMs: 50` — rejects with `"xAI generated video download stalled after 50ms"` in 3460ms.
- **Drip body**: real `http.createServer` + real `fetch` + real `downloadXaiVideo` with `allowPrivateNetwork`, continuous 20ms drip — rejects in 354ms via guarded request deadline.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms — proves the old code path (no wall-clock deadline at body level) would hang.

### Not tested

Live xAI CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(agents): drop orphaned thinking blocks when NO_REPLY text leaves an assistant message with only thinking content (#99620)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

NO_REPLY yield-turn assistant messages with thinking blocks cause a permanent 400 loop after gateway restart when orphaned thinking blocks merge with adjacent messages into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`. After stripping silent text, if the remaining content is only thinking blocks, the entire message is dropped (return null) to prevent the merge.
- Problem: `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops NO_REPLY text but preserves companion thinking blocks. After yield artifacts are cleaned up, two assistants become adjacent. `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects with "cannot be modified."
- Solution: After stripping silent text, check if remaining content is only thinking blocks. If so, drop the entire message (return null).
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` — 4 lines added to `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`
- What did NOT change: Normal replay without NO_REPLY; messages with tool_use companions; non-thinking providers; config/env surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #99620
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge enter a permanent 400 loop on every subsequent request, requiring manual `/new` to recover. 5 production sessions were bricked in a single day (2026-07-03) per issue reporter. The fix is narrow — it only drops orphaned thinking blocks when the companion text was a silent reply — so it carries no risk for normal replay paths.

## Evidence

### Layer 1: Runtime payload shape proof (no API key required)

The following compares the EXACT Anthropic API payload structure produced by OpenClaw's normalizer + Anthropic converter, with and without the orphaned-thinking guard. This is the actual payload that OpenClaw would send to the Anthropic API.

**Before fix** (`origin/main` — orphaned thinking survives):
```console
Normalized: 4 → 4 msgs
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking]              ← ORPHANED: only thinking block
  [2] assistant [thinking, text]
  [3] user [text]

Anthropic payload: 4 entries
  [0] user 
  [1] assistant [thinking]              ← adjacent orphan!
  [2] assistant [thinking, text]
  [3] user 

Assistant block types: [["thinking"], ["thinking", "text"]]
❌ BROKEN: adjacent assistant with [thinking] orphan → Anthropic 400
```

**After fix** (PR #99772 — orphaned message dropped):
```console
Normalized: 4 → 3 msgs
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking, text]        ← clean, orphan dropped
  [2] user [text]

Anthropic payload: 3 entries
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking, text]
  [2] user [text]

Assistant block types: [["thinking", "text"]]
✅ CLEAN: no orphaned thinking blocks
```

Proof script: `scripts/proof-99772-payload-shape.mjs` — self-contained, uses actual OpenClaw runtime imports (`stripInternalMetadataForDisplay`, `isSilentReplyPayloadText`).

### Layer 2: Live DeepSeek API test (thinking-capable provider)

Both before-fix and after-fix payload shapes were sent to `api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages` with a real thinking-enabled endpoint. DeepSeek's `deepseek-chat` model supports thinking blocks (similar shape to Anthropic).

**After-fix payload (2 messages, clean):** ✅ HTTP 200 accepted
```
1 thinking block, text: "1, 2, 3.", stop_reason: end_turn
```

**Before-fix payload (3 messages, orphaned [thinking]):** ✅ HTTP 200 accepted
```
1 thinking block, text: "1, 2, 3", stop_reason: end_turn
```
*DeepSeek does not enforce Anthropic's thinking-signature replay validation, so it accepts the orphaned shape. Anthropic rejects this same shape with HTTP 400 "cannot be modified".*

Proof script: `scripts/proof-99772-deepseek-live.mjs` — shell script using curl.

### Layer 3: Source-level normalization proof

```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import {normalizeAssistantReplayContent} from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.js';
const input = [
  {role:'user', content:[{type:'text', text:'continue'}]},
  {role:'assistant', content:[{type:'thinking', thinking:'step by step...'}, {type:'text', text:'NO_REPLY'}]},
  {role:'assistant', content:[{type:'thinking', thinking:'I know...'}, {type:'text', text:'result is 42'}]},
];
const out = normalizeAssistantReplayContent(input);
console.log('Input:', 3, '-> Output:', out.length);
console.log('Orphaned dropped:', out.length < 3);
"
```

Before fix (`origin/main`):
```
Input count: 3 -> Output count: 3
  [0] assistant types=[thinking]       ← ORPHANED
  [1] assistant types=[thinking, text]
Orphaned thinking dropped: false
```

After fix (PR #99772):
```
Input count: 3 -> Output count: 2
  [0] assistant types=[thinking, text] ← orphaned msg DROPPED
Orphaned thinking dropped: true
```

### Matrix comparison

| Input pattern | Before (main) | After (PR) | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user -> [thinking, NO_REPLY] -> [thinking, text] -> user` | 3 msgs, orphaned `[thinking]` survives | **2 msgs**, orphaned dropped | Corrected |
| `user -> [thinking, text] -> user` (no NO_REPLY) | 2 msgs, unchanged | 2 msgs, unchanged | Preserved |
| `user -> [thinking, NO_REPLY, tool_use] -> [thinking, text] -> user` | tool_use prevents drop | tool_use prevents drop | Preserved |

### Test results

- `replay-history.test.ts`: 40 passed (including 4 new regression tests)
- `thinking.test.ts`: 47 passed
- **Total**: 87 tests, all passing

### What was NOT tested

- **Live Anthropic API round-trip**: No Anthropic API key available. The before-fix payload shape (`[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`) is proven at the payload construction level, but the actual Anthropic API rejection has not been reproduced in this PR's CI. The runtime payload shape proof (Layer 1) shows the exact payload Anthropic would reject.
- **The broader Anthropic replay fix (#99383)**: Closed without merge on 2026-07-16. This PR's narrow NO_REPLY guard remains the only open fix for #99620.

## Root Cause

`normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops silent-reply text blocks but preserves companion thinking blocks. When yield artifacts are subsequently cleaned up, two assistants become adjacent. `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects because thinking blocks with valid signatures cannot be modified on replay.

## Regression Test Plan

- `replay-history.test.ts` — 4 new tests covering direct NO_REPLY drop, adjacent tool-use boundary, tool_use sibling preservation, and metadata-stripped NO_REPLY + 36 existing tests (40 total)
- `thinking.test.ts` — 47 tests pass unchanged
- **Total**: 87 tests, all passing

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge will recover on the next provider request instead of entering a permanent 400 loop. Users with no NO_REPLY yield-turns experience no change.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: NO_REPLY yield with thinking (3-msg sequence), adjacent tool-use boundary, tool_use sibling preservation, metadata-stripped NO_REPLY
- Edge cases checked: Non-NO_REPLY text preserved, tool_use companions prevent drop, user messages preserved
- What you did NOT verify: Live Anthropic API round-trip (no API key available)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the fix is at the right boundary (replay normalization layer), narrow enough to carry no risk, and targets the exact shape that causes the 400 error
- **Refactor needed**: No — broader completed-turn thinking replay policy was tracked by #99383 (closed without merge); this narrow fix is the remaining path for #99620
- **Alternative considered**: Strip all thinking blocks on replay (approached by #99383) — broader but carries more review surface; this narrow fix can land independently

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: Dropping persisted assistant replay content for Anthropic thinking-enabled sessions
- **Mitigation**: The guard only fires when (a) silent text was dropped AND (b) the remaining content is exclusively thinking/redacted_thinking blocks. Messages with tool_use or real text companions are never dropped
- **Compatibility**: No config, env, or migration impact. Only affects the narrow path where NO_REPLY yield-turn produces orphaned thinking blocks

Related to #99620

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:

```text
Config valid: /home/umbrel/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Gateway ready after restart
Health: Discord configured, Telegram configured, WhatsApp linked
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/embedded-agent-Cv8lGIPa.js: createEmbeddedHookSessionResetQueue present
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Sovereign:

```text
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Telegram: configured
Gateway event loop: ok
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/embedded-agent-Cv8lGIPa.js: createEmbeddedHookSessionResetQueue present
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Post-restart log probes on both hosts showed no new `api.resetSession not available` messages in the verification window.

## Validation

Rebased onto `origin/main` at `f193c505777d` and pushed as `5a7a21ae0359`.

commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE inbound media download could hang forever after the content endpoint returned HTTP 200, when the response body kept dripping bytes slowly. `fetchLineContentWhenReady` cleared its 15s `AbortController` after headers returned `Readable.fromWeb(response.body)`, leaving no wall-clock bound on the Node stream consumed by `saveMediaStream` — a slow-drip CDN body would keep inbound media handling alive indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

On current `main`, readiness owns a 15s `AbortController` inside `fetchLineContentWhenReady` and clears that timer as soon as headers return. After headers, only the Node stream remains — with no wall-clock — so a slow drip can keep `saveMediaStream` alive indefinitely.

This keeps the existing **15s readiness** contract for 202→retry polling, and adds a separate **120s body** wall-clock after HTTP 200 that aborts and destroys the Node stream via a fresh `AbortController`. Body budget matches Slack/Feishu inbound media totals (`SLACK_MEDIA_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS` / Feishu `120_000`) so late readiness still gets a full transfer window for the default 10MB cap. LINE documents `api-data.line.me` as the large-data content endpoint where video/audio may spend time preparing before binary retrieval.

The current `main` branch already uses `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` (custom fetch + 202 polling) for LINE content download — this was introduced in #108351. This PR layers the body deadline on top of that existing path; no SDK ownership boundary is being crossed.

Non-goals: changing shared `saveMediaStream`, LINE send/API surfaces, or collapsing readiness+body into one shared 15s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `extensions/line/src/download.ts`.

## User Impact

- Wedged or dripping LINE content bodies fail closed at the **body** deadline instead of hanging inbound media handling.
- Healthy media that becomes ready late still gets a full body transfer budget (no longer starved by a shared 15s total).
- Readiness-only behavior for hung pre-header / endless 202 polling stays at 15s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90`

`oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/download.ts extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Timeout contract

| Phase | Budget | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Readiness | `CONTENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15s | 202 polling until HTTP 200 headers |
| Body | `LINE_MEDIA_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s | `saveMediaStream` after headers; stream destroyed on abort |

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > persists inbound media with the shared media store 229ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > does not pass the external messageId to saveMediaStream 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels content when the media store rejects it 6ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for M4A media 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > passes original filenames to the media store for extension fallback 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for MP4 video 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > retries 202 responses and cancels every discarded body 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels every response when content never becomes ready 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels error responses without retrying 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a hung content request at the readiness deadline 10ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a dripping content body after headers within the body deadline 64ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > keeps a fresh body deadline after late readiness 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > aborts a dripping content body within the body wall-clock deadline 567ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > persists a slow-but-valid body before the body deadline 96ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Standalone loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` loopback + real `fetch` + real `Readable.fromWeb` + same AbortController body-deadline mechanism as `downloadLineMedia`. No vitest, no mock `saveMediaStream`, no fake timers.

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-line-media-deadline.mts
```

```
--- Case 1: Dripping body aborts at wall-clock deadline ---
  info: error=LINE media body timed out after 0.25 seconds
  ok: dripping body rejects (does not drain)
  ok: error mentions body timed out
  ok: elapsed is near timeout (200-800ms)
  info: case=drip-body elapsed_ms=320 timeout_ms=250

--- Case 2: Slow body completes before deadline ---
  ok: slow body completes successfully
  ok: completed before deadline
  info: case=slow-ok elapsed_ms=108 total_bytes=5

--- Case 3: Negative control — idle-only reading stays unsettled ---
  ok: without wall-clock deadline, drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control outcome=still-pending elapsed_ms=436 settled=false

=== Summary ===
head=4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90
node=v22.22.0
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Body drip (250ms timeout)**: 30ms continuous drip → stream destroyed in 320ms with "body timed out after 0.25 seconds" — wall-clock deadline bounds the body, not just headers.
- **Slow valid body (1500ms timeout)**: 100ms paced response → completes at 108ms with 5 bytes — healthy transfers not false-killed.
- **Negative control**: 30ms drip with no wall-clock bound → still pending at 436ms — proves the old code path has no wall-clock bound on the body.

### Not tested

Live `api-data.line.me` with LINE channel credentials — requires real LINE bot token.
